lines.description: Chuckles greeting: 'Ho eyo he hum, I've got a clue! It's important, and just for you!'
Chuckles says: "Why, I'm Chuckles the jester, of course! You've heard of me haven't you? Sure you have!"
Chuckles says: "You've heard a word? Why that's absurd!"
Chuckles describes his job: "To jape, to jeer, to prance, to frolic! To keep this place unmelancholic!"
Chuckles says: "I practice tomfoolery for Lord British - or anyone else who passes too close."
Chuckles says: "And jeer!"
Chuckles says: "And prance! To dance a Corybantic dance!"
Chuckles says: "Jeer and prance! Prance and frolic!"
Chuckles says: "I lurch 'round like an alcoholic!"
Chuckles says: "'Cause Dick and Harry both called in sick."
Chuckles says: "Call him Mr. Nose... But don't tell him I said so!"
Chuckles says: "Shhh! Don't let him know I told you!"
Chuckles says: "If hints were mints and mints were hints, think what a world it would be!"
Chuckles says: "A quest, a chest, oh what a jest!"
Chuckles says: "To teach, to preach, what waste of speech!"
Chuckles says: "I just said that!"
Chuckles says: "You just said 'that!'"
Chuckles says: "Oh, he's no fun."
Chuckles says: "I'll show you fun before I'm done!"
Chuckles fallback response: "Ho ho, hee hee, thou art funnier than me! To ask a jester of <Last Input>!"
Chuckles says: "Yes, it's crucial to your quest. Do you want to know what it is?"
Chuckles says: "Perhaps I don't want to tell you!"
Chuckles says: "Perhaps I'll tell you anyway!"
Chuckles asks: "Do you think I will?"
Chuckles says: "How foolish of you to think so!"
Chuckles says: "Congratulations! You're exactly right!"
Chuckles says he will not tell the clue.
Chuckles offers a hint that may lead to the clue.
Chuckles says: "Search the chest in Nystul's room."
Chuckles asks about the nun, the dragon, and the drunken penguin joke.
Chuckles gives the no-response to the penguin joke.
Chuckles says maybe you can teach him the joke someday.
Chuckles says he tried to amuse or confuse you.
Chuckles asks whether you enjoyed his jokes.
Chuckles says he will have to try harder.
Chuckles asks why Dupre is like a horseshoe.
Chuckles gives the horseshoe punchline.
Chuckles says he will tell another joke.
Chuckles asks the goose/avatar riddle.
Chuckles explains that the riddle answer flow was wrong.
Chuckles restarts the goose riddle.
Chuckles gives the goose punchline.
Chuckles asks what you thought of that joke.
Chuckles responds defensively to the joke reaction.
Chuckles admits he was the one who asked.
Chuckles gives his good-cheer closing rhyme.
Lord British initial greeting: Avatar! 'Tis good to see thee again.
Lord British verifying the Avatar's identity.
Lord British asks about the Compendium as proof of identity.
Lord British confirms the Avatar and gives the key.
Lord British explains that the same key opens the sewers under the castle.
Lord British begins explaining what has transpired since the Avatar's last visit.
Lord British begins recounting the collapse of the vast underworld from which the Avatar rescued him.
Lord British says there are still forces of evil abroad in the land.
Lord British explains that Britannia is under attack by gargoyles.
Lord British says the gargoyles have been coming up through the dungeons.
Lord British explains that the gargoyles have mainly attacked the shrines.
Lord British mentions the Shrine of Compassion falling.
Lord British tells the Avatar to ask Sir Geoffrey about the mission.
Lord British says a room has been set aside for the Avatar.
Lord British describes the Avatar's room in the west wing of the castle.
Lord British says his servants placed equipment there for the Avatar.
Lord British says the Avatar may borrow anything in the castle if needed.
Lord British offers healing whenever the Avatar needs it.
Lord British explains that asking him to repeat will replay the explanation.
Lord British notices the Avatar has misplaced the castle key.
Lord British gives another castle key.
Lord British asks what the Avatar would speak of.
Lord British identifies himself.
Lord British says he sits once more upon the throne of Britannia.
Lord British describes the burden of ruling in troubled times.
Lord British says the gargoyles are the greatest threat the realm has ever known.
Lord British says fate has brought the Avatar in Britannia's hour of need.
Lord British hopes the Avatar can drive the gargoyles back.
Lord British says all efforts so far have failed.
Lord British warns the gargoyles may have captured all the shrines.
Lord British urges the Avatar to hurry and foil the gargoyles' schemes.
Lord British urges commitment to the eight virtues.
Lord British says belief in the virtues separates Britannians from the invaders.
Lord British identifies Geoffrey as Captain of the Guard.
Lord British recognizes the black stone.
Lord British says he did not know there were more such orbs.
Lord British says the stone will serve the Avatar well if mastered.
Lord British explains how to use the stone to open a gate.
Lord British says the stone's placement is the key.
Lord British explains that proper placement conjures gates to many destinations.
Lord British tells the Avatar to ask the leaders of each town.
Lord British says: "I collect rare books."
Lord British says: "There's one in particular I've been hunting for many years."
Lord British says: "It's called 'The Wizard of Oz.' Ever heard of it?"
First part of Lord British's request to bring him The Wizard of Oz if found.
Second part of Lord British's request: he would appreciate the Avatar bringing the book to him.
Lord British says he has promised a great reward to whoever brings him a copy.
Lord British says the Avatar is carrying too much for him to reward properly.
Lord British tells the Avatar to bring the book back later, when less burdened.
Lord British farewell: "May fortune favor thee."
Lord British says: "I cannot help thee with that."
Lord British asks the Avatar to bring him The Wizard of Oz if it is found during the Avatar's travels.
Lord British says he has promised a great reward to whoever brings him a copy.
Lord British says the Avatar is carrying too much to receive the reward properly.
Lord British tells the Avatar to bring the book back later when less burdened.
Lord British says: "Thou hath found a copy!"
Lord British says: "Long hath I anticipated this moment..."
Lord British says: "Not since my childhood have I read this wondrous story."
Lord British says: "Here is your reward."
Lord British asks: "Who told thee of that nickname!?"
Lord British says: "Well, I'd rather thou didst not call me that."
Lord British directs the Avatar to ask Tholden about Compassion.
Dupre greeting: "Yes, <Avatar Name>?"
Dupre says: "It's Dupre - sounds like dew pray, remember?"
Dupre says: "Why, questing, of course! We've been on many a quest together, you and I."
Dupre says: "Yes, you've gone on some really fine ones."
Dupre says: "When you're not around I have to settle for rescuing damsels, finding grails, and the like."
Dupre says: "It could be worse."
Dupre says: "Some of them are pretty eager to show their gratitude, if you know what I mean..."
Dupre says: "Wink wink, nudge nudge, say no more..."
Dupre says: "That's right."
Dupre says Lord British likes to keep grails around for banquets.
Dupre says Lord British will throw a feast if the gargoyle invasion is dealt with.
Dupre says: "They may be the toughest threat we've ever faced."
Dupre says: "I've been with you since the start of this quest, haven't I?"
Dupre says Lord British ordered him not to leave your side until the quest is complete.
Dupre says: "Besides, you know how I hate to miss a good quest."
Dupre says: "Please, let's not talk about ducks..."
Dupre says: "Yes, enough chit chat. Let's go find some action!"
Dupre says: "Ask Iolo about that."
Guard introduction: "Hello. Can I help you with something?"
Guard says: "Well, what can I help you with?"
Guard refuses to give out his name.
Guard says he is one of Lord British's elite guards.
Guard hails Lord British, Britannia, and the Avatar.
Guard says their ranks have thinned in the war against the gargoyles.
Guard says few are left to patrol the cities.
Guard says: "I fear we may lose this war."
Guard says not a single shrine has been liberated.
Guard says he has noticed a resemblance between gargoyles and daemons.
Guard says patrolling cities is their only job in times of peace.
Guard says: "May we see such times again!"
Guard says he will return to his duties.
Guard says: "Perhaps you should ask somebody else."
Shamino greeting: "Yes, my friend?"
Shamino gives his full name.
Shamino says: "I help my friends when they need it."
Shamino says he prefers to spend the rest of his time exploring the woods.
Shamino says he still considers the Avatar one of his closest friends.
Shamino says: "I prefer the Deep Forest."
Shamino says Spiritwood is not as dense and has strange wisps everywhere.
Shamino says: "It is home to me."
Shamino says he loves walking in the dark shadows of the trees and studying forest creatures.
Shamino says: "A home needs not walls to make it so."
Shamino says that when folk ask why he has no walls, he asks where the trees are in theirs.
Shamino says trees are the lifesblood of the realm.
Shamino says woodland creatures have lives of their own, more interesting to him than townfolk.
Shamino says there is much to be learned from animals, if you will but listen.
Shamino says he knows little of wisps' nature, but some mages have investigated them.
Shamino suggests asking one of the members of the council.
Shamino says he feels Lord British does not understand the gargoyles' true nature.
Shamino says he knows Lord British better than you might think.
Shamino says he will follow wherever the Avatar chooses to lead.
Shamino says the Avatar needs his guidance through the wild parts of Britannia.
Shamino says it is a pleasure to assist the Avatar.
Shamino says the Avatar should ask Dupre about that.
If Dupre in party : Dupre says "Now Shamino's going on about talking to animals... The whole world's going batty!"
Nystul introduction: "Hail to thee <Gender>, and well met."
Nystul says he learned of the Avatar's peril through his mystic arts.
Nystul tells Iolo he saw the book.
Nystul asks to examine the book.
Nystul says he had hoped Iolo might take the book to Mariah for translation.
Nystul reacts to examining the book.
Nystul describes the book cover showing a gargoyle standing over a slain human.
Nystul says the book is interesting.
Nystul says the book is written in a language he does not know.
Nystul tells the Avatar to take the book to Mariah at the Lycaeum.
Nystul says Mariah has studied many languages and may decipher the book.
Nystul introduces one more topic for the Avatar.
Nystul says he noticed the Avatar arrived through a red gateway.
Nystul asks whether the Avatar has the stone that opened the gate.
Nystul wonders where the stone could have come from, perhaps the gargoyles.
Nystul tells the Avatar to ask Lord British about the stone.
Nystul says Lord British has some knowledge of such items.
Nystul says such items are quite rare.
Nystul says the only such item he has seen is the one Lord British possesses.
Nystul asks whether the Avatar has gone to the Lycaeum and shown Mariah the book.
There is naught else I can help thee with at this time.
Geoffrey says: "Thou hadst best speak to Lord British before aught else."
Geoffrey says: "I'm glad to see thee, <Avatar Name>. Perhaps thou canst prevail where others could not."
Geoffrey says he sent a party of ten to recapture the Shrine of Compassion from the gargoyles.
Geoffrey says: "Alas, they failed dismally."
Geoffrey says the survivors are recuperating in the town of Cove.
Geoffrey says: "Thou wouldst do well to speak with them first."
Geoffrey says: "Mayhap they learned something which might aid thee."
Geoffrey says: "I must confess I fear the worst."
Geoffrey says: "The gargoyles are such powerful foes, and they are spreading so fast..."
Geoffrey says: "Perhaps the end of the realm is nigh."
Geoffrey says: "Good luck, and my prayers go with thee."
Geoffrey says: "Best not waste time talking..."
Geoffrey says: "Who knows what acts of villainy the gargoyles are comitting even as we speak?"
Geoffrey says: "I hope you've had a chance to visit Cove and speak with Gertan."
Maldric initial greeting: "Excuse me a moment."
Maldric asks: "Now, what were you saying?"
Maldric interrupts: "Wait a minute,"
Maldric recognizes the Avatar.
Female Avatar line: Maldric says he knew she must be the most beautiful woman in Britannia.
Male Avatar line: Maldric says the Avatar is the greatest hero in the land.
Female subsequent visit greeting.
Male subsequent visit greeting.
Maldric gives his name and says he was once Maldric the boar hunter.
Maldric says he used to live in the forest and hunt wild boars.
Maldric tells of how he was hired
Maldric clarifies he means Lord British himself.
Maldric says those were good times, but he is happy in the castle.
Maldric says the secret is in the spices.
Maldric refuses to reveal the family recipe.
Female Avatar line: Maldric says he is tempted to tell.
Maldric explains that he cooks for those who live in the castle and Lord British's guests.
Maldric says the work is satisfying, but at times he wishes he could travel with one such as the Avatar.
Maldric says Lord British has many friends.
Maldric describes the castle as a fancier home than any his family lived in.
Female Avatar line: Maldric wishes his old hut were still there so he could invite her to spend an evening by the fireplace.
Maldric says: "There's fire enough in my kitchen, but 'tis no place for romance."
Maldric says: "I shouldn't even speak of such things."
Maldric says: "After all, you are the Avatar, and I but a lowly cook. Please forgive me."
Maldric says: "He's a good man. Likes plenty of pepper in his stew."
Maldric says: "Spice puts some variety in life, is what I always say."
Female Avatar line: "You're a pretty spicy little number yourself!"
Maldric says: "Yes indeed."
Maldric says: "I've heard about all of your adventures. I wish I were a warrior too, and not just a cook!"
Maldric says: "I like having a job where I can make people happy."
Maldric says: "See you later. And next time you dine with his majesty, I'll cook you something special."
Maldric says: "Funny you should mention that... It reminds me of my secret recipe for roast boar."
Sherry initial visit squeaking.
Sherry response to squeak.
Sherry response to squi/nitt/fibl.
Sherry frightened response.
Sherry says: "I am Lord British's friend, Sherry."
Sherry says Lord British reads her bedtime stories every night.
Sherry says Lord British knows the one about Hubert the Lion by Heart.
Sherry says: "That's my favorite story."
Sherry says: "Pleased to meet you!"
Sherry says: "Give me some cheese and ask me again."
Sherry says: "I can slip through openings that are too small for you to fit through!"
Narration: "The mouse wiggles its whiskers at you."
Sherry says: "You're funny!"
Sherry asks: "Do you have any cheese?"
Sherry says: "Oh, that's too bad."
Sherry says: "I don't smell any cheese!"
Sherry asks: "Can I have some?"
Sherry says: "Well, you're no fun."
Sherry goodbye line before she has properly talked.
Sherry says: "Come visit me again soon!"
Sherry says: "Thank you very much!"
Sherry says: "I can help you! Do you want me to come with you?"
Sherry says: "Ok."
Sherry says: "Great!"
Sherry says: "Boats make me seasick."
Sherry says: "With that many people I'd get trampled!"
Sherry says: "Travelling with you is fun! I hope we find some more cheese soon."
Sherry asks whether the Avatar wants her to go home now.
Sherry says: "I'm not leaving until we get out of this thing!"
Sherry says: "Okay."
Sherry says: "All right. Now I can hear my bedtime stories again!"
Sherry sneezes: "Kerchew!"
Sherry says: "I'll leave my stuff with you in case you need it."
Sherry says: "I wish people would clean up under their beds and cabinets..."
Sherry says: "Dust mice are no friends of mine!"
Sherry reacts at Dr. Cat's line about feeding her to his pets.
Sherry reacts when Phoenix throws a dagger at a little mouse.
She's had more time to develop her musical talents than I all these years.
But after this quest, I hope to join her in Minoc and enter the Artisan's Guild.
There always seems to be a quest when you come to visit us, doesn't there?
Iolo's the only name I remember having.
Yes, it's always been a hobby of mine.
Sometime you should just drop by for tea.
All right, make it Frazier's Folly, then.
A drink worthy enough to greet an old friend.
Not as big as Britain, but it's a peaceful town.
I've been a crossbow maker for so long I've gotten weary of it.
Well, do you need help with something, or maybe you've got time for a story, eh?
If you want me to gather all our gold together so you can carry it, just say so.
Or I could split it up evenly, if you prefer.
My hut is in the deep forest south of Yew.
My horse Smith lives there.
Hopefully, now that my apprentice has taken over the shop, I'll be able to spend more time as a bard.
My shop still sells the finest crossbows in the land.
I've done a lot over the years to refine the design, and I trained my apprentice well.
I'm sure she'll carry on the tradition in fine fashion.
Have you heard the piece "Stones" that I composed some years ago?
It's one of my favorites.
That's too heavy for you, but I'll let you have it anyway.
None of us are carrying any gold.
This is all you can carry right now.
You're carrying enough already, I think.
But we have no gold!
We don't have enough gold to bother with.
But maybe I shouldn't tell you about that. After all, I did promise.
Iolo, you promised never to tell anyone about that!
Though there is still need for the instruments of war, as I grow in years I would now take up those of peace.
You know where Mr. Nose hangs out?
Remember, he doesn't like people to call him that.
I've been with you since we saved you from those gargoyles, haven't I?
They're pretty ugly-looking, if you ask me.
His nibs, the king, told me I should stay with you constantly.
I'll make an exception when you have to relieve yourself, of course.
My favorite one is the time when I had to wake Dupre up for a tournament.
Yes, you're right. I'm sorry.
Ask me later when he's not around.
I've still got to tell you that story about Dupre sometime.
Ask Shamino about that.
Ask Shamino about that.
Ask Shamino about that.
Oh, you should get my wife Gwenno to teach it to you sometime.
Kytyn will never believe it when I tell her I got to meet the Avatar in person!
It's so nice of you to come by and talk to me!
My father ran the mint before me, but I get lonely here sometimes.
Copper pence, silver pieces, and gold crowns, they're all made right here.
Anyway, I just wanted to tell you that I always hoped someday I'd meet a man like you.
Oh, I'm sorry, I wasn't listening. I was just noticing how strong and handsome you are.
It really was delightful talking to you.
It's Terri. Don't you think that would be a good name for an Avatar's wife?
Anyway, I just wanted to tell you that I always wanted to grow up to be just like you.
You probably wouldn't remember her, but she was at the big celebration right after you recovered the Codex.
By royal decree, I am the only one allowed to mint the official coinage of the realm.
My mother used to tell me stories about you when I was a girl.
Say, aren't you the Avatar? Yes, I recognize you from your portrait.
Hello, my name's Terri. I run the mint.
But since you're the Avatar, I'll give you a full hundred crowns for every stone's weight of gold you have.
Normally, there's a ten percent tax on the exchange.
We must be mistaken. But let me know if you come across any gold nuggets later.
Well, if you do later, you know where to find me.
Do you have any gold nuggets you'd like to trade in for crowns?
I get most of my gold from people who bring in nuggets to exchange them for coins.
Oh, I'm sorry. I wasn't listening. I was just thinking how nice it must be to be as beautiful as you.
It's Terri, but I wish I had been named after you.
And maybe if you have time for it, I could show you more than a few silly coins.
I know you're very busy saving Britannia and all that, but I hope you'll come and visit me again.
You should visit there sometime. But please stay and talk to me a bit longer first!
She's a good friend of mine. She runs the museum.
My mother told me all about it.
Of course, we have you to thank for bringing us the Codex and saving Lord British.
Britannia has been so prosperous lately that there's been a lot of demand for gold coinage.
Here, let me show you.
Of course, I'm sure you only carry gold crowns with you, being as important as you are!
May she rest in peace.
Oh, you've come back to visit me again!
I'm eating right now. Come see me at the mint sometime and we can chat.
May he rest in peace.
You must be the bravest person I've ever met. I can't believe it's really you!
I entrusted them with the rune due to their compassionate nature.
As for the other runes, they are no longer together, as they were when the Codex was recovered.
Since then, they have become scattered throughout the land. Each was sent to a town near its shrine.
Thou must ask the lords of each of these towns. They should be able to tell thee more.
The towns are Moonglow, Jhelom, Yew, Minoc, Trinsic, Skara Brae, and New Magincia.
It is the greatest treasure in all the realm.
It was founded by Lord British
I hope I have been of assistance.
I cannot help thee with that.
I have so many markers to keep, festivals to plan. I am so busy. But I can spare you a moment.
I am Tholden von Brillius, Chancellor to Lord British.
In my younger days, I was known as the werecat of the wine cellar.
I could tell you stories, but there's no time for that now.
A fine ruler indeed. 'Tis a pleasure to keep his kingdom running smoothly for him.
All the little details of governing, all the paperwork falls on my shoulders.
Someone must do it, and yet I miss the days when I was a carefree adventurer.
The rune and the mantra of compassion are in the keeping of the bards at the conservatory.
I can't tell you much about that. Lord British donated it to the museum, but I can't get him to talk about it.
From what little he says, I think it's an artifact from his home world.
There is a great deal of knowledge available there for the serious scholar.
Be sure to look at our paintings while you're here, and come again soon.
We're expecting some unicorn horns and a Klein bottle from Trinsic.
I can't help you with that. Try the library at Lycaeum.
Hello and welcome.
My name is Kytyn.
Perhaps that explains why I like birds.
I used to be a falconer.
That was before Lord British appointed me to my current position.
A true gentleman if ever I saw one.
I'm the curator of the Royal Museum of Oddities.
It's just one of the projects Lord British has funded to provide a better life for his people.
He also established a conservatory that shares a building with the museum.
The roads that span the realm are his doing as well.
Sometimes I can hear their music drifting through the walls.
Usually that noisy, crackling field drowns it out, though.
It's very pretty.
Travel is much easier these days.
That's for sure.
I can tell you about any of the exhibits you're interested in.
We have the monolith, the energy fields, the perpetual motion machine, the bones of Zog, the mystery fountain, and the dragon's head, wings, and eggs.
Which one were you curious about?
This skeleton seems about ten times older than any other found in Britannia.
Surely it has much to tell us about our origins, if we only knew what it meant.
Someone named Gertan donated all these parts.
I think he said something about a dragon named Freytag.
If you want to ask Gertan, I think he's in Cove.
Somebody found a huge boulder with a jet of water spraying out of it.
We had it magically transported here, buried with its surface flush with the ground, and then we built this building on top of it.
Of course, we left a hole in the floor for the water to spray through.
I often drink from it when I'm thirsty. The water is quite good, but there's something strange about it.
It vanishes somehow before it hits the ground.
That's a very curious device. The motion of each gear turns another until eventually the movement is propagated back to the same gear again.
There's one thing I can't figure out.
We've made plans of the device, but I can't see how they started it moving in the first place.
None of the gears were turnless, all the others were already going.
What's worse, the motion serves to hold the machine together.
If the gears were still, the whole thing would fall apart. How it was built is quite a mystery.
The field is generated by a curious spell.
By some process not yet understood, it converts magical energy into electrical energy, producing a continuous discharge.
If we understood this process better, it would probably lead to all sorts of useful applications.
Her name is Nan. Whatever you do, don't say anything to her about spiders!
She has quite an imagination. Sometimes she lets it carry her away.
I asked you not to wear it out. It's the only name I've got.
My wife and I teach young bards the art of composition, performance, and improvisation.
Tell me, what does it mean?
Hmm, no, I don't think that's it.
Until we meet again
I like the confused look on your face too much to ruin it by telling you.
Dost thou know what it means?
Nobody I know does either!
I've been trying to work the mantra of compassion into a song, but I don't know what "moo" means.
Ariana has the rune, and they could have hardly found a sweeter child to give it to.
Once in a great while, a student comes along with such a gift for learning that one need but offer a little guidance and step back to watch them learn.
To have such students is the most rewarding part of a teacher's job, and Ariana is one such.
Welcome, I am Sir Kenneth, and I'd gladly play a song for thee.
Kenneth's my name, don't wear it out.
Usually it doesn't give her any trouble.
Yes, I know of the Rune and Mantra of Compassion.
We also give concerts on occasion.
Bards must be well versed in such matters.
With my lute
Every time I pick up my lute, spiders crawl out of it.
There must be hundreds of them nesting in there!
I hate spiders! They're creepy, ugly, disgusting things. Why won't they leave me alone?
She's very talented. She'll go far, if the spiders don't get her.
Fare thee well and watch thy step, the spiders are lurking everywhere.
I cannot help thee with that.
Now, now, my dear, have you forgotten about the gloves I gave you?
I am Lady Nan.
The mantra of Compassion is Mu. Is that a spider on your shoulder?
No, 'tis just a trick of the light.
'twas given to our most promising student, young Ariana.
I would play for thee, but I'm worried about my lute.
Oh, yes. Perhaps if I wore those I could play.
Iolo gave them to me for my birthday.
Yes, I know the Rune and Mantra of Compassion.
Why, making music, of course!
Matt here had a most unfortunate accident as a child that left him deaf and dumb. I'd suggest you ask his wife instead.
Which one of you?
Which item?
That costs gold!
Interested?
but would make thee overburdened.
Excellent!
But thou hast not enough gold.
Thou hast not enough gold.
But I think I can trust thee with credit, just this once.
I'm sorry, but I cannot offer more credit, even to thee.
The Gargoyle Wars make my wares much in demand.
How goes business, Gwenneth?
Of course, 'tis still called Iolo's Bows out of respect for the master.
Yellow!
And thy companions as well.
I heard rumors that you were in town.
Very well. Very well indeed. Sir Geoffrey himself just placed quite a large order.
Much demand for bows these days, what with the gargoyles.
And what can I do for Iolo's friend this fine day?
I recognize thee. Thou art Iolo's friend.
What can I do for thee?
Hello again, what can I do for thee?
What'll it be next?
What a strange question! I'm Gwenneth, of course.
Just ask Iolo.
But dost thou not know Yolo?
Well, I am his former apprentice, Gwenneth.
Once I was Iolo's apprentice, but then he decided to retire.
Now 'tis my shop, and I craft the bows sold here.
I hear from the soldiers that the gargoyles are fierce opponents.
Some gargoyles move like the wind itself and can strike you like lightning bolts.
The gargoyles also have a strange and terrible weapon.
It is called a boomerang, and it is a most bizarre ranged weapon.
It flies out to strike its target, then returns to the hand that threw it.
Against such magic, the soldiers chose to arm themselves with good, stout Britannian bows.
I would not wish to speak of Yello amongst his friends.
I might embarrass him.
Nay, I really would not wish to speak of my master behind his back.
I usually do I carry those in stock.
There has been a shortage of late because of the Gargoyle war.
Go see Lynne the fletcher over to the north.
Alina is a fine fletcher and usually keeps me supplied with arrows and bolts
